You want the best for your audience.

I’ve attended a number of trauma trainings during my years as a therapist. Each of them sadly fit into two ineffective categories:

  1. They teach about trauma by using shock value. (This isn’t necessary.)
  2. They teach about the biology of trauma... But wow, it gets boring! (I promise it can be more engaging.)

Your audience deserves the best.

I make learning about the Polyvagal Theory and trauma informative, fun, & interactive.

  • Live Polling
  • Mixed Media: You’d be surprised at how effective a clip from the Office can be at showing defensive autonomic states or how Ferris Bueller’s Day Off can be the perfect example of vocal prosody.
  • Discussion: I use both large group and small group discussions to elicit connections with audience members and real-world applications of ideas.
  • Fun “Experiments”: I include audience activities to experience state shifts live, like talking to a partner while the other is not allowed to show facial expressions!

Clarity, simplicity, & shared language.

I want the same thing you do - the best possible experience and deepest learning for your audience. I ensure that through two fairly simple standards for myself...

  1. If I have to rely on shock value, I’m underserving the audience.
  2. If I can’t teach simply, I don’t understand deeply.

These standards have driven me to learn and practice at a level most others shy away from. My content audience, clients, and colleagues consistently tell me I make complex ideas clear and simple. I do the same thing for live audiences, whether virtual or in person.

Let’s collaborate!

I love teaching and am thrilled to connect with you to discuss your audience’s needs and how we can create an impactful experience together.

Whether you’re looking for a keynote on the intricacies of the Polyvagal Theory, a workshop on trauma recovery, or a personalized training session, I’ll bring clarity and practical solutions to your event’s audience.

Who I love presenting to

The short answer is - everyone!

But more specifically, I love presenting to mental health providers who have never heard of the Polyvagal Theory. I get so much out of seeing the lightbulbs go off in peoples’ minds as their eyes light up. I love hearing them share about new ideas and understandings.

These moments of clarity and insight are deeply fulfilling for me. I hope to bring these experiences to your people!

Here is a list of some people I have presented to:

  • County mental health workers
  • Nurses
  • Police
  • Foster parents
  • Teachers and school administration
  • Yoga studio
  • Collegiate therapy students
